title: Dedicated migration tactical heatmap - seller kit (draft)
content:
Purpose: one-pager + quick talk-track for sellers to qualify and accelerate Hosted -> Dedicated migrations. This is a tactical heatmap (seller-facing) not the full exec brief — think: where to push for a pilot, what levers to use, and compact rebuttals for ops/infra objections.

Status: draft. Use as companion to the reserved capacity negotiation playbook; contains rough thresholds and seller notes. Add metrics from account telemetry before sharing with the buyer.

High-level framing (for pitch intro)
- Problem: companies scale beyond predictable per-token economics and need isolation, predictable throughput, and stronger SLAs.
- Redwood promise (short): Dedicated -> predictable throughput, isolation, and priority capacity with Canary/rollback controls.
- One-liner value prop for engineers: "Same API, dedicated GPUs — consistent latency, cost predictability, and private compute footprint."

Heatmap axes (how to use)
- X axis: Business urgency (Pilot -> Production)
- Y axis: Ops friction (low -> high)
- Cells map buyer profile + seller tactic + one primary KPI to move the deal

Heatmap cells (seller playbook)
1) Top-right (High urgency, High friction) — Enterprise platform teams
- Signal: security audit, compliance clause, SLA asks, spike pricing concerns.
- Tactic: Lead with Private vs Dedicated decision tree. Offer 3-week pilot on Dedicated with dev-only network ACLs and audit export (sample). Attach quick SOW template.
- KPI to move: time-to-first-validated-PII-free-run (days).
- Script snippet: "We can stand up a dedicated pool with reserved capacity and a short SLO timeline for audit readiness — pilot typically takes 2–3 weeks including key rotations."

2) Top-left (High urgency, Low friction) — Product-led scale-ups
- Signal: high token volumes, bursty traffic, developer advocates pushing for predictability.
- Tactic: Price framing: show predictable monthly commit vs variable hosted spend. Offer short-term burst credits and autoscaling floor.
- KPI: predicted monthly spend variance reduced to <15%.
- Script: "If your token spikes are causing bill surprise, we model a commit that drops unit cost while keeping burst buffer."

3) Bottom-right (Low urgency, High friction) — Regulated / Fintech/Health
- Signal: legal hold, encryption-at-rest questions, on-prem preference.
- Tactic: Push compliance checklist + optional private deployment intro, highlight KMS/HSM integrations. Offer compliance discovery session with solutions eng (free 1-hour).
- KPI: compliance redline items identified and resolved.

4) Bottom-left (Low urgency, Low friction) — Early product experiments
- Signal: small teams, prototype workflows, cost-conscious.
- Tactic: Recommend Hosted but with caching, infer-optimize plan. If convincing, propose low-commit Dedicated pilot for throughput testing.
- KPI: latency SLOs measured at <200ms p95.

Operational objections & quick rebuttals
- "We can't commit to reserved spend" -> Offer a stepped commit (1-quarter ramp) + burst buffer; show modeled crossover point from hosted to dedicated at current QPS.
- "What if model mix changes?" -> Explain model pinning + dynamic routing; discounted fallback to compatible variants and Canary rollout.
- "Security/audit" -> Provide audit artifacts checklist and reference architecture for VPC + KMS; offer compliance discovery call.
- "Latency concerns" -> Share recent p95 numbers from comparable workloads; suggest a short production-mirroring pilot with synthetic traffic.

Seller enablement assets to attach (toggle as needed)
- Mini-ROI table: current hosted spend vs predicted commit (two scenarios: steady QPS, bursty QPS).
- One-page SOW skeleton for 30-day dedicated pilot.
- Engineering checklist: network, keys, model pin list, eval prompts.
- Sample rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback.

Pilot qualification checklist (sales to fill out quickly)
- Estimated daily tokens: ___
- Peak QPS: ___
- Required latency p95: ___ms
- Compliance class: (none / moderate / high)
- Decision-maker (infra/security): name, email
- Timeline preference: immediate / 30d / >60d

Quick numbers (placeholders — replace with account data)
- Break-even commit example: if monthly tokens > 15B, dedicated commit likely cheaper by ~28%.
- Typical pilot length: 2–6 weeks for infra + 2–4 weeks for production validation.

Tactical negotiation nudges
- Offer upgrade credits for first 3 months if they sign >X commit (use finance playbook).
- Package observability add-on (90-day retention) as a pilot differentiator for platform teams.

Open items / notes to solutions eng
- Need a canned canary policy example tailored to large models (link to GH PR).
- Request: 1-page network diagram for on-prem pattern (Marco to draft).
- Audit artifact pack: collate HSM/KMS docs + SOC2 excerpt (Priya to pull).

Next steps for seller using this heatmap
1) Fill pilot qualification checklist and add to GTMP Jira ticket.
2) Request solutions eng slot for technical handshake (use booked-playbook link).
3) Attach ROI table with account token metrics; run economics model (spreadsheet link).

Notes / voice-of-customer fragments collected in discovery
- "We just saw a 4x spike and our API started failing — we need predictable throughput."
- "Our security team won't sign without dedicated logs and a KMS flow."
- "We like Redwood hosted but can't forecast monthly spend for investor budgeting."

References and quick links
- Internal: reserved-capacity-negotiation-playbook-qa-draft (see pricing levers)
- Confluence: /spaces/GTM/pages/DEDICATED+MIGRATION
- Jira: GTMP-1283 (pilot sales task)

End of draft. Add real account numbers and swap placeholders before sharing externally.
